name: Senegal
summary: Senegal taxes residents on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 43%, with no unilateral relief for foreign tax. Foreign dividends and, per Deloitte, capital gains fall under that scale; some share gains are taxed at 25%, and Senegalese dividends bear 10%. There is no wealth tax, and Deloitte describes only a fixed XOF 25,000 duty on accepting a succession; gift duties were not verified. Confidence is low: no tax authority source was reachable and the 2026 code reform was not reviewed.

regimes.name: Senegalese tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide income tax at 0-43%; 10% WHT on Senegalese dividends; no wealth tax; fixed duty on successions.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if the permanent home or permanent residence, the main professional activity, or the centre of economic interests is in Senegal. Non-ECOWAS citizens need a residence card.

capital_gains.summary: Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Capital gains of individuals are taxed at the progressive income tax rates (0-43%) on declaration, real-estate gains are collected at source by the notary, and gains on the sale of shares are taxed at 25% 'in certain cases' (Deloitte 2026). Which rule applies to a resident's gains on foreign listed securities is not stated; scored at the 43% top progressive rate.

sources.title: Senegal - Individual - Taxes on personal income

capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Progressive scale (XOF, annual): 0-630,000 0%; to 1.5m 20%; to 4m 30%; to 8m 35%; to 13.5m 37%; to 50m 40%; above 50m 43%; household 'shares' (quotient) system.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The 25% rate for some share disposals is thought to be the CGI art. 259 levy (older sources); its scope for listed and foreign shares is unverified. A reform of the Code général des impôts for 2026 was mentioned in search results but not reviewed; whether it changed individual investment-income rules was not checked.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign listed securities and foreign real estate: 0.43, the top progressive rate that Deloitte gives as the capital gains rate for individuals. Domestic listed shares and private business shares: null because the 25% share-gain rate applies 'in certain cases' that could not be identified (the range is 25-43%). Senegalese real estate: null because the notary's at-source rate was not found.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading gains are business income at progressive rates.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation; Senegal grants no unilateral foreign tax relief, only treaty relief (Deloitte).
open_questions: Which share disposals qualify for the 25% rate and whether it covers listed or foreign shares; the at-source rate on real-estate gains.
Whether foreign gains of individuals are actually taxed at progressive rates in practice.

dividends.summary: Senegalese dividends bear a 10% withholding tax for residents and non-residents. Foreign dividends of residents fall into worldwide income at progressive rates up to 43%, and Senegal gives no unilateral credit for foreign tax (treaty relief only).

sources.title: Senegal - Individual - Taxes on personal income

dividends.exemptions_thresholds: See the progressive scale under capital gains.
dividends.important_exceptions: Whether the 10% WHT on Senegalese dividends is final (libératoire) for individuals is supported only by older (2006-era) code text and was not confirmed for the current code. A reform of the Code général des impôts for 2026 was mentioned in search results but not reviewed; whether it changed individual investment-income rules was not checked.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 10% WHT treated as final. Foreign: 43% top progressive rate on worldwide income, no unilateral credit; treaty credit only where a treaty applies (Senegal has more than 30 treaties, mostly African and European).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% on dividends to residents and non-residents, reducible by treaty for non-residents.
dividends.treaty_network: More than 30 treaties; BEPS MLI in force from 1 September 2022 (Deloitte). Includes France; no US treaty, so US dividends bear 30% US WHT.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 30%; dividends received outside the participation exemption are taxed after a 60% abatement. Not modelled.
open_questions: Whether foreign dividends are taxed at progressive rates or at a proportional rate (as for domestic investment income) was not verified.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth or net worth tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land/property tax not researched; transfers of real property bear a 5% registration duty (Deloitte).

inheritance.summary: Deloitte reports only a fixed registration duty of XOF 25,000 on deeds accepting a succession or legacy; no proportional inheritance tax is described. Treatment of gifts (donations) to children was not found.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Fixed XOF 25,000 per deed of acceptance of a succession.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Registration duties on donations inter vivos and on transfers of Senegalese real estate by succession were not verified; the PwC summary does not cover inheritance or gift tax. A reform of the Code général des impôts for 2026 was mentioned in search results but not reviewed; whether it changed individual investment-income rules was not checked.
inheritance.gift_tax: Not verified: registration duties on donations to children could apply.
open_questions: Registration duty on gifts (donations) to children and on inherited Senegalese real estate not verified; the 'no inheritance tax' scoring rests on one professional summary.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual has a permanent abode or permanent residence in Senegal, carries on a professional activity there (other than a subsidiary one), or has the centre of economic interests there (PwC). No day-count test is stated.

routes.name: Residence card
routes.requirements: Non-citizens staying long term need a residence card (carte de résident); ECOWAS citizens have free movement. No residence-by-investment programme identified. Not researched in detail.

corporate.summary: 30% CIT (15% for free export companies and special economic zones); minimum tax 0.5% of turnover when loss-making (capped XOF 5m). Participation exemption for qualifying dividends; 10% WHT on dividends.
corporate.special_zones: Special economic zones and free export companies at 15%.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed; Senegal's tax on foreign dividends and gains (up to 43%) exceeds US long-term rates, so Senegal would be the binding layer. No US-Senegal income tax treaty.
open_questions: Senegal's DGID website and the current Code général des impôts could not be reached; figures rest on Deloitte (April 2026) and PwC (August 2026) summaries.
